newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to pull Lake's name for CIA post.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to pull Lake's name for CIA post.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday decided to withdraw the nomination of his first-term national security adviser Anthony Lake to head the Central Intelligence Agency, an administration source said.

"He met with the president today and the president very reluctantly, and after trying to convince Tony to fight it, accepted his personal judgment that he ought to withdraw his nomination," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

Asked why Lake had decided to withdraw himself from consideration for the CIA post, the source replied: "His belief that the committee would delay endlessly ... and that the president would be deprived of a director of central intelligence."

The surprise decision came after three days of intense Senate confirmation hearings, in which lawmakers questioned Lake's integrity, management skills and fitness to head the CIA. The hearings were set to resume this week.
The source added that Lake had become convinced that the committee would "nibble him to death rather than deal with the nomination straight-up anytime soon."

The source said that Lake had proposed withdrawing his name before last week's confirmation hearings, but had been dissuaded. He added that Lake had written an "eloquent" letter explaining his reasons for stepping aside.
